#5056. Prop Firm Payouts Near $2 Billion: 10 Best Prop Firms In 2026

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Prop firm payouts are approaching the $2 billion mark, with data from Payout Junction showing nearly $1.97 billion in cumulative payments across 45 tracked firms since October 2023. More than $115 million has been recorded in November 2026 alone.

The figures offer a glimpse into how large the funded trading industry has become. But finding the best prop firms in 2026 requires looking at something payout leaderboards rarely tell you: what traders actually have to go through to get paid.

A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown gives a trader just $3,000 of room for error. Add consistency requirements, withdrawal caps and restrictions on trading strategies, and two accounts with identical advertised balances can offer very different trading conditions.

The industry is also expanding beyond its traditional forex and futures markets. New platforms are introducing prop trading for cryptocurrencies and tokenized stocks, giving traders access to a wider range of markets without having to commit the full advertised account balance themselves.

For this guide, we examine ten prop firms across forex, futures and cryptocurrency markets, looking beyond advertised profit splits to compare evaluation rules, trading conditions, costs and payout eligibility.

Editorial disclosure: This guide is based on published trading rules, product documentation and available payout data. Traders can lose their challenge fees, and most retail funded trading programs initially use simulated accounts. Receiving a payout is not guaranteed.

The firms are grouped by their suitability for different trading styles rather than ranked by a single payout leaderboard.

According to Payout Junction’s November 24 data, approximately 1.19 million payout transactions have been matched to public blockchain records since October 2023.

The tracker covers 45 firms, although its figures do not necessarily represent all payments made by those businesses. Bank transfers and other payments outside its blockchain tracking coverage may not appear in the dataset.

November has already recorded roughly $115.5 million in tracked payments across more than 91,000 transactions.

These are substantial figures, but they need context.

A firm paying out $50 million does not necessarily offer a better opportunity than one paying out $5 million. The larger business could simply have more customers, higher fees or a larger number of accounts.

Chart by NewsBTC, data from Payout Junction, November 16–22, 2026. Tracked blockchain payments only.

Nor do the figures tell us how much traders collectively spent on challenges, resets and subscriptions before receiving those payouts.

Without that information, it is impossible to determine the industry’s aggregate profitability for traders.

Payout data is useful evidence that payments have occurred. It is not evidence that the average customer makes money.

That distinction matters when comparing the following firms.

FTMO offers a conventional two-phase evaluation for traders who prefer clearly defined profit objectives and fixed overall loss limits.

Its two-step model requires a 10% profit target during the first phase and 5% during verification.

The maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial simulated capital, while the overall loss limit is 10%.

For a $100,000 evaluation, that translates into a $10,000 first-phase profit target and a $10,000 maximum overall loss allowance.

FTMO also offers a separate one-step model. Traders should not assume that its rules are identical to the traditional challenge.

The two-step structure may appeal to traders whose strategies require more breathing room than accounts with narrow trailing loss limits.

The first-phase target, however, requires meaningful performance relative to the allowed drawdown.

FTMO is worth considering for traders with an existing, tested forex or CFD strategy. Its two-step structure is easier to assess mathematically than many trailing-drawdown alternatives, although that does not make it easy to pass.

FundedNext operates across CFDs and futures, offering several routes to funded-style trading.

Its Stellar 2-Step model is particularly interesting for traders who want a traditional evaluation with relatively conventional risk limits.

The first phase requires an 8% return, followed by 5% in verification. Both phases apply a 5% daily loss limit and 10% maximum overall loss.

The published rules specify five minimum trading days per phase.

The firm also offers alternative CFD challenge formats and futures evaluations.

One area worth examining is its performance reward policy. Reward frequency and eligibility can vary according to the option selected, with some routes requiring a specific number of profitable trading days.

This makes comparing the headline profit split alone insufficient.

FundedNext’s strongest feature is choice. Its biggest complication is also choice. Traders should compare the funded-stage conditions of each product before deciding which evaluation to purchase.

FundingPips offers several evaluation models, including one-step, two-step and evaluation-free alternatives.

Its 2-Step Standard model requires an 8% profit target followed by 5% in verification.

The firm’s current documentation also confirms that the previous optional 10% first-phase target was discontinued on July 24, 2026.

FundingPips is an example of why traders must pay attention to changes in prop firm rules.

Its Standard model documentation applies a 35% consistency condition to the on-demand reward cycle.

This means a trader who generates most of their profit during one unusually successful session could need additional trading before qualifying for a withdrawal.

That might suit a strategy producing relatively steady returns. It could be less suitable for traders whose profits are concentrated around a handful of strong market opportunities.

FundingPips deserves consideration for its payout flexibility, but traders should examine the conditions attached to their preferred withdrawal cycle rather than choosing whichever option advertises the highest reward share.

The5ers offers several forex-focused evaluation and account-development programs.

Its High Stakes program is built around a two-stage evaluation and subsequent growth opportunities.

The firm distinguishes between different versions of High Stakes, making it important to identify the exact account being purchased rather than relying on older comparisons.

The appeal of The5ers is its focus on account development over time.

Traders who already have a strategy capable of producing steady returns may find growth-oriented programs more interesting than accounts designed primarily around rapid evaluations.

However, scaling opportunities should not be treated as guaranteed increases in accessible trading capital.

The trader must meet the conditions attached to the program, and trading restrictions continue to apply.

The5ers is a reasonable candidate for patient forex traders who value gradual account development. Its suitability depends on the precise High Stakes version and the trader’s ability to satisfy its growth criteria.

Hola Prime offers multiple evaluation formats across forex, CFDs and futures.

Its 2-Step Prime challenge requires an 8% profit target during the first phase and 5% during the second, with at least three trading days in each phase.

The firm’s published schedules also differentiate risk limits according to account size.

Hola Prime’s product range gives traders alternatives to the standard evaluation experience. However, account fees, platform access and withdrawal terms differ across models.

Its advertised challenge-fee refund also comes with conditions. Under the reviewed 2-Step Prime terms, the refund is distributed across the first four successful payouts rather than returned immediately upon passing.

That is an important detail for anyone calculating how much they need to earn before recovering their initial expenses.

Hola Prime is worth comparing if trading platform choice matters to you. Just remember that a fast payout-processing promise begins after a withdrawal becomes eligible, not necessarily after your first profitable trade.

Topstep is focused on futures trading through its Trading Combine and subsequent funded-account structure.

Unlike a traditional CFD evaluation, the maximum loss allowance is relatively small compared with the advertised account size.

Its published Trading Combine parameters include maximum loss limits of $2,000 for a $50,000 account, $3,000 for a $100,000 account and $4,500 for a $150,000 account.

A trader purchasing the $50,000 option is not receiving $50,000 that can be lost while testing a strategy. The relevant initial risk allowance is $2,000.

After passing the Trading Combine, traders can progress to an Express Funded Account, which is a simulated funded-stage account.

Its payout policy includes conditions relating to withdrawal eligibility, payout limits and changes to the maximum loss threshold after withdrawals.

Topstep is worth considering for futures traders who prefer a structured environment. Anyone moving from forex prop trading should first understand how dollar-based trailing loss limits differ from percentage-based static drawdowns.

Tradeify offers futures evaluations with different routes into funded-stage trading.

Its Select evaluation does not impose a daily loss limit during the evaluation but does apply a consistency requirement.

After passing, traders choose between Select Flex and Select Daily payout policies.

The ability to select a payout arrangement is attractive because not every trader earns profits in the same way.

A trader producing relatively consistent daily returns may prefer a different structure from someone whose strategy depends on occasional larger moves.

However, the choice is permanent for that funded account, according to Tradeify’s official payout policy.

Changing to the alternative arrangement requires obtaining another qualifying account.

Tradeify’s Select model is particularly interesting because it allows traders to choose how they want to approach withdrawals after evaluation. That flexibility is only valuable if the trader understands both options before selecting one.

Take Profit Trader offers futures trading programs built around an evaluation, a simulated PRO account and potential progression to a live-market PRO+ account.

The firm published updated plan information on November 23, 2026, making older descriptions of its account rules particularly important to recheck.

Its current product announcement describes three-day evaluations, frequent PRO withdrawals and no funded-stage consistency rule under the new plans.

The buffer is the detail traders should examine most closely.

The firm allows eligible traders to withdraw profits above the required buffer. Consequently, a trader can have a profitable account without necessarily being able to withdraw all that profit while retaining the account.

Legacy accounts may also remain subject to their original terms.

Take Profit Trader stands out for its withdrawal model. Traders interested in frequent payouts should still calculate how much profit must remain in the account before treating those earnings as spendable income.

Lucid Trading offers several futures account models, including LucidPro, LucidFlex, LucidDirect and LucidDaily.

Its LucidFlex program is particularly relevant to traders who want to avoid funded-stage profit-concentration restrictions.

According to the firm’s LucidFlex documentation, the funded account does not impose a consistency rule or a separate payout buffer.

The published profit-sharing arrangement is 90% for the trader.

The absence of a consistency rule does not mean traders can withdraw unrestricted amounts whenever they choose.

LucidFlex still has specific payout conditions, including requirements that must be satisfied before a withdrawal is approved.

Traders must also consider how a payout affects the account’s maximum loss threshold.

LucidFlex may appeal to traders who dislike having their profitable sessions constrained by a consistency formula. That makes the account more flexible in one respect, not necessarily less risky overall.

HyroTrader focuses on cryptocurrency traders rather than adapting a traditional forex evaluation to include a limited selection of digital assets.

Its one-step program requires a 10% profit target, with a 4% daily drawdown and 6% maximum overall loss under the published model.

The firm also offers alternative evaluation formats, including its recently introduced lower-cost Hyro Core program.

The attraction is that traders can use crypto-oriented trading infrastructure and market data rather than relying exclusively on a conventional forex platform.

For traders unfamiliar with derivatives, our guide to long and short positions in crypto explains how leverage and liquidation affect market exposure.

HyroTrader’s trading rules also clarify that allocated challenge and funded-account balances are simulated. Payouts represent a contractual share of eligible simulated trading performance.

That distinction matters because the term funded account is frequently misunderstood.

HyroTrader is worth examining for traders who already specialize in crypto markets. It is less compelling for someone whose only reason for choosing crypto is the belief that higher volatility makes a challenge easier to pass.

There is no single account structure that suits everyone.

These selections reflect specific published product features, not independently measured payout approval rates or guarantees of superior results.

The advertised account balance is usually one of the least informative numbers in a prop firm comparison.

Account A offers twice the advertised balance of Account B. Yet it provides less room for losses and requires a substantially higher profit relative to that allowance.

This does not establish the probability of passing either challenge. That depends on the strategy, trading costs, risk management and other account rules.

It does show why choosing the largest advertised account is not always sensible.

The calculation becomes more complicated when an account uses trailing drawdown.

A static maximum loss threshold remains anchored to a specified balance under the account’s rules.

A trailing drawdown moves upward as the trader generates profits, potentially reducing the room available for a subsequent losing streak.

Intraday trailing drawdown is particularly important because some models adjust the threshold based on unrealized profits.

A trade that briefly gains $1,000 before closing with a much smaller profit can therefore affect the trader’s remaining loss allowance.

Two firms advertising the same maximum drawdown can offer very different practical conditions depending on how and when that threshold moves.

Passing an evaluation is generally only the first stage.

The rules that determine whether someone receives a withdrawal can be more restrictive than the initial profit targets.

A consistency rule limits how much of the qualifying profit can come from a single trading session or another defined period.

For example, suppose a trader earns $2,000 during their best day and finishes the payout cycle with $4,000 in qualifying profit.

That best day represents 50% of the total.

Under a hypothetical 40% consistency requirement, total qualifying profit would need to reach at least $5,000, assuming the best day remains unchanged and the rule uses this particular calculation.

The trader may have to continue trading even though they are already profitable.

Some firms require profits to remain in an account as a buffer against future losses.

Others limit how much traders can withdraw during their initial payout cycles.

These restrictions are not necessarily unreasonable. A firm may want traders to demonstrate sustained performance before allowing larger withdrawals.

But customers should know exactly what they are buying.

There is a considerable difference between advertising daily payouts and allowing a trader to withdraw every dollar earned that day.

Account agreements can restrict copy trading, certain automated strategies, cross-account hedging, account sharing, news trading and other trading behaviors.

The precise definitions differ between firms.

Before paying for an account, traders should review both the public trading objectives and the account agreement governing payout eligibility.

A strategy permitted during evaluation may have different conditions after funding.

The advertised challenge price is only the initial expense.

Depending on the firm and product, customers may also incur subscription charges, reset fees, funded-account activation fees, market-data fees, platform costs or withdrawal-processing charges.

Promotional discounts can make the first purchase attractive without necessarily reducing the cost of subsequent attempts.

Consider a hypothetical trader who purchases four $100 challenges before successfully qualifying for a funded account. That trader has spent $400 before accounting for any additional charges.

The first $300 payout would not mean the trader has made a net profit from prop trading.

Their total challenge expenditure would still exceed their withdrawals.

This is another reason the industry’s approaching $2 billion payout milestone should not be confused with $2 billion in net trader earnings.

Our editorial assessment considers the following factors:

The selection is based on documentary research rather than a claim that NewsBTC has personally purchased, traded or withdrawn money from every program.

Reported payouts are considered supporting evidence of industry activity, not a standalone measure of reliability.

Retail prop firms generally offer traders access to an evaluation or simulated trading program in exchange for a fee.

Belgium’s financial regulator, the FSMA, has also published a consumer warning about retail prop trading programs, highlighting the risks of paying for repeated challenges.

Participants who meet the contractual requirements may receive monetary rewards linked to their trading performance. Some businesses subsequently move qualifying traders into live-market accounts.

This is different from opening a conventional brokerage account with personal deposited trading capital.

It also means traders should examine who operates the program, which legal entity they contract with, where disputes are handled and what happens if the provider changes its rules or ceases operations.

A large number of successful payout transactions does not guarantee that every valid withdrawal will be approved, nor does it establish the financial health of the company.

Before buying a challenge, traders should read the current agreement, establish their eligibility and understand which circumstances can lead to account termination.

FTMO and FundedNext are worth comparing for traditional forex evaluations. Topstep, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader and Lucid Trading offer different futures trading structures, while HyroTrader is focused on cryptocurrency.

The most suitable firm depends on the trader’s strategy, risk tolerance, market preference and withdrawal requirements.

Take Profit Trader offers daily eligible withdrawals under its reviewed PRO model, subject to the required buffer. Tradeify also offers a Select Daily payout arrangement.

Daily availability does not remove other eligibility conditions.

LucidFlex does not impose a funded-stage consistency rule under its published terms. Take Profit Trader’s new PRO plans also advertise no funded-stage consistency requirement.

Evaluation-stage restrictions may still apply.

HyroTrader is one of the crypto-focused firms worth researching because its programs are built around digital-asset trading.

Traders should compare cryptocurrency market access, drawdown calculations, exchange integrations and payout eligibility before selecting a program.

Yes. Traders can lose evaluation fees, subscriptions, reset fees and other charges without ever receiving a payout.

The simulated nature of many funded accounts does not eliminate the financial risk of paying for repeated evaluations.

No. Withdrawals depend on the firm’s contractual requirements, trading-rule compliance and ability to make payments.

Historical payout figures do not guarantee future withdrawals.

The prop trading industry has grown considerably, and nearly $2 billion in tracked payouts demonstrates that substantial sums are changing hands.

What it does not demonstrate is how many traders are profitable after accounting for their expenses.

The best prop firm is not necessarily the one paying the most money, offering the largest account or advertising the highest profit split.

It is the one whose evaluation and funded-stage rules are compatible with a trader’s existing strategy.

Before purchasing a challenge, calculate how much room the account actually provides for losses, how much profit must be generated before a withdrawal becomes possible and how much repeated attempts could cost.

Those numbers are considerably more useful than the advertised account balance.

#5055. Google's Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in 'Impossible' Game

Google's Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in 'Impossible' Game

Google says its Willow quantum processor won a mathematical coordination game 98.3% of the time, above the 88.9% maximum attainable by classical strategies, in a Science study published Thursday.

The experiment tests quantum contextuality, so measurement outcomes depend on what else is measured alongside them. Google researchers explained that “you cannot assign fixed, pre-existing values to everything you might measure.”

Don’t panic. The result does not mean Google has a commercial quantum computer, nor that its largest experiment beat every classical machine. The 98.3% figure came from four qubits—the basic unit of information used to encode data in quantum computing—the 105-qubit run tested a different, more limited challenge.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Google with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The first test used the Mermin-Peres magic square game, which asks two players to fill intersecting parts of a three-by-three grid without communicating. Their answers must obey conflicting row-and-column rules and match at the shared square.

A prearranged classical strategy can succeed on no more than eight of nine assignments, or 88.9%. Entangled qubits can theoretically win every round, while Google’s physical processor won 98.3% across 900,000 trials, according to the researchers.

The researchers wrote that “our qubits coordinated better than any pre-written table allows.” Unavoidable hardware noise prevented the result from reaching the quantum ideal.

Google also measured contextuality. Any model with predetermined outcomes scores at most 4; quantum theory allows 6. Willow registered 5.590, with a reported uncertainty of 0.008.

A separate GHZ parity game asked up to 71 entangled qubits to deliver coordinated binary answers. Success was measured against the strongest classical winning rate, which approaches 50% with more players; Google remained above that limit throughout its tests, despite accumulating hardware noise.

Researchers also verified genuine entanglement across 45 qubits. In the hidden linear function task, a shallow quantum circuit had to produce a binary string satisfying mathematical constraints. The processor reached roughly 60% success using 105 qubits.

Google says the tasks exposed small, systematic errors that conventional randomized tests can hide. Its corporate blog called contextuality testing “a sensitive new method to catch subtle hardware errors,” potentially helping engineers evaluate circuits used for chemistry and materials research.

The work follows Google's October report of a 40-fold error reduction in preparing magic states, a resource needed for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

For Bitcoin, the looming danger is that a future fault-tolerant quantum computer could break digital signatures, but that is still far from happening. Google’s 105-qubit task was instead a shallow mathematical circuit, and its largest instance still failed in about four out of 10 runs.

The Monday New York trading session open brought a flurry of volatility to Bitcoin [BTC] and the rest of the market. Nvidia’s stock soared 31% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately.

Combined with the oversold market conditions, the tech and AI-sector stock market bounce helped Bitcoin rally to a local high of $64,603.

Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.

At the time of writing, BTC was back below the $61,000 mark. Its rally liquidated $520.89 million in short positions across the crypto market, including $225.58 million for Bitcoin alone.

The BTC spot ETF flows on Monday measured -$60.4 million, extending the bearish market sentiment and highlighting the lack of demand.

The MVRV Z-score measures the difference between market capitalization and realized capitalization. It displayed a reading of 0.24 and has fallen by 0.11 over the past week, reaching among the lowest in four years.

It has remained positive for 1,410 days, reported crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. A drop below zero would mean that the market cap has fallen below realized cap, a sign of deep capitulation.

Another metric that reached some of its lowest levels in four years was the supply in profit. It compares the market price with the last moved price of coins in the circulating supply.

Less than half of the coins are in profit, mirroring the lows from the previous bear market lows of late 2022.

In August, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on Binance peaked at +2.41b. This peak showed heavy market buying as prices climbed toward $80k. Yet, as the price pushed to the local high at $87k, the CVD on Binance declined to -6b.

This was a bearish divergence; rising sell market orders captured take-profit behavior, while late entrants and leverage hunts pushed prices higher.

In November, across all exchanges, the CVD’s decline accelerated alongside price drawdown, and Binance’s CVD figure reached -21b, wrote crypto analyst FundingVest.

If the falling CVD momentum slows down while Bitcoin’s price continues its descent, it could be a constructive sign that will considerably increase the chances of a recovery.

#5051. $600K stolen from Trezor and Exodus wallets – How did it happen?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Onchain Lens reported over $600,000 lost from one user’s Trezor and Exodus wallets on the 23rd of November. The Trezor wallet theft report raised a harder question: how did transfers use the victim’s signing authority without their claimed approval?

The blockchain investigator listed approximately $580,000 in Tether [USDT] losses on TRON and $23,400 in USD Coin [USDC] on Solana. Another $9,500 reportedly disappeared from an Exodus wallet on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max.

Reportedly, the victim generated the recovery phrase on Trezor and kept it on paper and refused to allow anyone physical access to the device.

A 49,999 USDT transfer on the 21st of November used the TRON account’s default owner permission. It was a direct transfer, with no transfer from operation drawing on an existing token allowance.

On Solana [SOL], the examined instruction identified the victim’s wallet as the transfer authority, signer, and fee payer. Notably, no separate delegate appeared.

These transfers used the wallet’s signing authority. However, it is unclear how someone gained that access.

A valid signature authorizes a transaction on the network. So, it cannot establish whether the owner knowingly approved it. The Trezor accounts on both chains shared one recovery phrase, making that backup a possible link between the losses.

In an X reply, Trezor said similar cases usually involved “a compromised wallet backup.”

It’s hard to say what happened here without more details.

The company asked the affected user to contact official support. Its reply offered a possible explanation, without establishing this incident’s cause.

Trezor says its Bluetooth chip cannot access private keys. On the other hand, Exodus says its Trezor integration also leaves those keys inside the hardware. Whether the user enabled that integration remains unclear.

Apple’s 9th of November update patched Bluetooth issues, but Onchain Lens found no evidence linking those vulnerabilities to these transfers.

Earlier incidents show why identifying the route matters.

As AMBCrypto reported, Trezor confirmed implants in three CryptoBilis-sold Safe 5 devices on the 12th of November. Those implants captured recovery words from device screens.

Separately, Confiant’s MoldyRoost research documented another route; malicious ads delivering exploits to vulnerable iPhones. Furthermore, Chainalysis counted roughly 158,000 personal-wallet compromise incidents affecting 80,000 victims in 2025.

For this user, the unanswered question is specific: how did someone obtain signing access across the affected wallets?

#5049. Bitcoin Rebounds to $61K After Weekend Plunge to Two-Year Low

Bitcoin Rebounds to $61K After Weekend Plunge to Two-Year Low

Bitcoin recovered to around $61,300 early on Monday after a turbulent weekend that saw it fall as low as $55,298, its lowest level since September 2024, as a slide in tech stocks and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy rattled risk assets.

The leading cryptocurrency was up 0.5% over 24 hours at time of publication, but down 4.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko data. It remains about 51% below its all-time high of $126,080.

The weekend low came a day after Bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday, as AI stocks slumped following Anthropic's IPO.

"Bitcoin's sharp volatility over the weekend was primarily the result of a steep pullback in U.S. tech stocks, expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve, and deleveraging across global risk assets," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, told Decrypt.

If growth expectations keep falling while inflation keeps the Fed hiking, "two key pillars that previously supported risk-asset rallies—ample liquidity and strong growth expectations—could be weakened simultaneously," Sun said. More than $2 billion in leveraged liquidations over the weekend had released some short-term selling pressure, he added, creating conditions for a possible rebound.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $669.2 million in net outflows on Friday, their largest single-day outflow since June 25, according to SoSoValue data. That brought last week's net outflows to $1.79 billion, the funds' third consecutive week of withdrawals topping $1 billion, and November's total so far to $4.14 billion, by Decrypt's calculation. Total net assets fell to $71.3 billion, the lowest since June 30.

"The weekend correction looks less like a Bitcoin-specific event and more like part of a wider market correction," Neil Steinhardt, head of Nexo U.S., told Decrypt, noting that gold and equities also fell. ETF outflows had worsened the drawdown, he said, adding that equities appeared to have led the sell-off.

It is now below its median since launch, while outflows run near $260M per day.

The last stretch this quiet, in mid-2024, came before the run to $100K. Periods of apathy tend to be better times to accumulate than periods of hype. pic.twitter.com/xiJ3HF9cLj

— glassnode (@glassnode) November 22, 2026

Onchain analytics firm Glassnode took a longer view. ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since the funds launched, while outflows are running near $260 million a day, the firm tweeted on Sunday. The last stretch this quiet, in mid-2024, preceded Bitcoin's run to $100,000, it said.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes struck a more bearish note. Bitcoin had "decisively" broken below its previous local low, he tweeted on Saturday, adding that "$50,000 will be the next real test" if the Nasdaq kept falling. On Sunday evening, as Nasdaq futures weakened in Asian trading, Hayes tweeted that Bitcoin could retest $55,000, and noted that South Korea's Kospi index had fallen 5%.

$BTC just decisively broke below the previous local low. If Nasdaq keeps puking, $50,000 will be the next real test. pic.twitter.com/vn0VSpuWAz

— Arthur Hayes (@CryptoHayes) November 21, 2026

On Decrypt Predict, users put a 17% chance on Bitcoin falling to $55,000 before the end of November, as of 5:56 a.m. ET on Monday. The market settles on Binance's BTC/USDT price, which fell as low as $55,130 last week, according to the Binance chart Hayes shared. Users put a 1% chance on Bitcoin climbing back to $82,500 this month.

Traders now turn to October's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, due on Wednesday, followed by the November jobs report on December 4 and the Fed's December 9 meeting.

The core PCE report "could help show whether the Fed is leaning toward 25 or 50 basis points," Steinhardt said, with markets then guided by the December meeting and comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and other officials.

Traders are leaning toward the smaller move. As of 6:00 a.m. ET on Monday, CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point hike on December 9 at 96.2%, up from 88.6% on Friday, with a 3.8% chance that rates stay unchanged. The odds of a half-point increase stood at zero, from 4.5% a week earlier.

U.S. spot selling remained heavy last week, according to a note from Bitfire Research shared with Decrypt. The Coinbase Bitcoin Premium Index, which tracks the gap between Bitcoin's price on Coinbase and on Binance, fell as low as negative 0.23%, the firm said.

Sun said he saw "no clear bullish catalyst" over the next one to two weeks, and expected Bitcoin to stay in a "high-volatility consolidation phase." Cooler inflation, steadier stocks and a return of ETF inflows could support a more sustainable recovery, he said, while hotter inflation and further tech losses could send Bitcoin back to its prior lows.

#5048. Bitcoin developers propose fix for transaction verification gap affecting Lightning wallets

The proposal would let lightweight wallets independently verify transaction signatures recorded in mined blocks, advancing efforts to standardize witness proofs across Bitcoin software.

Bitcoin developers have proposed a new verification system that would allow lightweight wallets to independently authenticate transaction signatures recorded on the blockchain.

The draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, submitted by developer Jean Pablo on Nov. 22, addresses a limitation in how wallets verify transaction information received from external servers.

The proposal could particularly benefit wallets such as Electrum, which supports Bitcoin's Lightning Network and relies on external servers for some blockchain information.

Currently, lightweight wallets can verify that a transaction was included in a Bitcoin block using a cryptographic proof tied to its transaction ID, or txid.

However, that identifier excludes witness data, which contains signatures and other information used to authorize spending under Bitcoin's Segregated Witness (SegWit) system.

Consequently, a wallet could successfully verify a transaction's inclusion while holding witness data that differs from what miners actually included in the block.

Pablo's proposal addresses this discrepancy by introducing standardized witness transaction inclusion proofs built around a second identifier, known as the witness transaction ID, or wtxid.

Unlike the conventional transaction ID, the wtxid incorporates witness data, allowing wallets to verify that the full transaction they received matches the version included in a mined block.

The proposed system connects that identifier to Bitcoin's existing witness commitment, which is recorded in the block's coinbase transaction. A second cryptographic proof then connects the coinbase transaction to the block header.

An ordinary proof checks the transaction ID. The draft adds a path from the witness data to the same block header.

A wallet can compare the witness data it received with what a valid block committed to.

The proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

The diagram follows the two proof paths described in the draft and the wallet verification flow in the Bitcoin Core discussion.

The proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

Together, these checks allow wallets to authenticate witness data without downloading and examining the entire block.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The development follows an earlier request from Electrum contributor SomberNight, who sought witness inclusion proofs to strengthen transaction verification for the wallet's Lightning Network functionality.

Lightning wallets interact with Bitcoin's underlying blockchain when opening, closing and monitoring payment channels, making reliable transaction information particularly important.

The proposed verification system would allow such wallets to independently confirm the witness data supplied by servers while continuing to operate without storing complete blockchain data.

The request previously prompted work on Bitcoin Core, where developers explored extending existing transaction proof commands to cover witness information.

That pull request closed in May without being merged, and developer Sjors Provoost later continued the effort through a separate implementation that introduced commands to generate and verify witness proofs.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin Knots introduced experimental witness-proof support in version 29.1, and Electrum developers have been working on related protocol changes.

However, these efforts use different proof formats, creating compatibility challenges between wallets and the servers providing blockchain information.

Pablo's proposal attempts to resolve those differences by specifying two binary formats and a JSON representation for exchanging and verifying proofs.

The first format provides a separate cryptographic proof for each transaction, while the second reduces duplicated information when verifying multiple transactions together.

In one example involving 10 transactions, the second format reduced proof data from 4,523 bytes to 3,325 bytes, approximately a 26% reduction.

The proposal also includes a Python reference implementation and 93 test cases designed to establish consistent verification behavior across software implementations.

Of those tests, 31 cover proofs that should be accepted, while 62 cover invalid proofs that verification software must reject.

The specification would give Bitcoin Core, Electrum and other wallet developers a common framework for implementing witness verification.

Pablo has requested feedback on the proposed formats and verification requirements, leaving developers to determine whether a shared standard can replace the experimental approaches already in use.

#5046. No CLARITY Act? How CFTC moves ahead with new crypto guidance

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Although the CLARTIY Act failed to pass the Senate this year, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) is working hard to develop new crypto market advisories.

On the 23rd of November, the agency issued a new advisory allowing certain crypto assets to be counted towards the financial resource requirements of regulated derivatives trading and clearing platforms. This includes Bitcoin [BTC], Ethereum [ETH], and payment stablecoins.

So now, Swap Execution Facilities (SEFs), Designated Contract Markets (DCMs), and Derivatives Clearing Organizations (DCOs) can use these digital assets to confirm that they have sufficient financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating expenses.

These requirements are designed to ensure that such platforms have enough funds to continue operating and meet their financial obligations, even during times of financial stress.

However, the approval comes with an important limitation. While eligible crypto assets can contribute towards the 12-month financial resources requirement, they cannot be counted towards the separate liquidity requirement. This is because, under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), cryptocurrencies are not classified as cash or highly liquid securities.

In simple terms, holding Bitcoin or Ethereum may help a platform prove its financial strength, but it cannot replace the cash or highly liquid assets it needs to meet immediate payment obligations.

The advisory also requires appropriate haircuts. In other words, the platforms must discount the value of crypto assets when calculating how much they can count towards their financial resources. This would be done to account for the price volatility and risks associated with digital assets.

Expressing their opinion on the matter, CFTC’s Chairman Mike Selig said,

Pleased to see @CFTC staff continue to provide important clarity around crypto assets in US derivatives markets through today’s staff advisory.

On the same day, though, the CFTC also introduced a new reporting framework for certain fully collateralized event contracts. This was done to replace the reliance on temporary regulatory exemptions and no-action letters that have been in place since 2017.

In other words, the move aims to make reporting requirements for event contracts, including prediction-market products, clearer and more consistent.

Yet, despite all the efforts, Senator Adam Schiff criticized the Trump-appointed CFTC Chairman over his handling of the legal battle surrounding prediction markets. Schiff claims that the chairman had previously told the Senate during his confirmation process that he would allow courts to decide whether prediction markets fall under gambling laws.

However, according to Schiff, the chairman has since acted against that commitment. Schiff believes that Selig has allegedly disregarded court orders and intervened in ongoing litigation in ways that favor the prediction-market industry.

His criticism suggests that the CFTC leadership is taking an active role in protecting prediction-market platforms rather than maintaining regulatory neutrality.

All of this coincided with the agency’s plans to use its existing authority to introduce two initiatives: Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM).

Solana Meme Coin for Fiona the Hippo Raises $100K for Cincinnati Zoo Charity

Fiona the Hippo, a fan-favorite pygmy hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, died last week after swallowing a hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure. Crypto bros have created a meme coin in her honor—raising $100,000 for charity in the process.

The tragic death came after a visitor tossed their knitted hat in the air, which then got caught by a ceiling fan and flung it through a small window into Fiona's habitat. The pygmy hippo lost her appetite as the hat got stuck in her small intestine, and veterinary staff tried their best to help Fiona pass the hat naturally—as surgery was deemed too risky. Unfortunately, Fiona died on Thursday, November 19, at nine years old.

As is often the case, crypto bros rushed to create a Solana meme coin that surged to a $3.52 million market capitalization the day after Fiona's death. It has since dropped more than 50% to $1.5 million, per DEX Screener.

Fiona the hippo has died after she ate a visitor's hat that fell into her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo. pic.twitter.com/YHbjoEEDhb

The Pump.fun-created token is donating 100% of the generated creator rewards to the Zoological Society of Cincinnati, the non-profit that runs the zoo and its scientific programs. So far, according to Donate.gg, $103,600 has been donated.

But, of course, profits are at the forefront of crypto traders' minds. One of the top traders turned a $1,637 investment into $43,800 in a matter of days, according to DEX Screener.

"I feel like animals are often treated more like attractions for people than living beings. Their safety and lives should come first, not just entertaining visitors," pseudonymous trader Athena Alpha told Decrypt. "This isn’t even the first time something like this has happened."

This sparked global outrage, as the gorilla was killed through no fault of his own. In turn, Harambe became one of the most viral memes of the 2010s.

"I think stricter action needs to be taken against both visitors and zoo officials to make sure things like this don’t happen again," the trader said. "Honestly, I feel like a big part of the problem is the lack of accountability and consequences. Unless people are held responsible, nothing is really going to change."

Fortunately, she survived this tough start to life and went on to become one of the zoo's most famous animals.

People's love for Fiona may have been boosted by the rise of Moo Deng, a cute pygmy hippo who went mega viral in 2024. As with Fiona, crypto traders made an unofficial meme coin for Moo Deng, but this one went much higher—peaking at a $610 million market cap.

Naturally, traders have made the comparison between the two pygmy hippos, with some suggesting that the Moo Deng meme coin's success should mean similar gains for the Fiona token.

With Fiona's meme coin sitting at a $1.5 million market cap, that thesis has yet to be proven.

"If Fiona goes to $1 billion, her legacy will live forever all around the world," one trader tweeted. "Do it for Fiona!"

Risk premiums on the weakest U.S. corporate bonds widened last week, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $570 million in net outflows on Monday.

U.S. junk-bond yields rose to 8.46% at the Nov. 20 close as investment-grade yields fell, according to ICE BofA data published Nov. 23 by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Bond investors demanded a bigger premium to own the weakest corporate debt. That gives Bitcoin buyers a separate gauge of risk appetite after Monday's rebound lost momentum.

The yield on the U.S. high-yield index rose from 8.25% on Nov. 16 to 8.46% on Nov. 20. The biggest yield move among the three corporate indexes was in bonds rated CCC or lower. Its effective yield rose from 17.88% to 18.61%.

Over the same dates, the investment-grade corporate yield fell from 5.95% to 5.84%. The two-year Treasury yield fell from 4.83% to 4.63%.

The gap over the Treasury curve widened across all three ICE BofA corporate bond indexes between Nov. 16 and Nov. 20, 2026.

The option-adjusted spread for bonds rated CCC and lower widened 92 basis points, compared with 42 for high yield overall and 8 for investment grade.

CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index. Option-adjusted spreads measure the yield premium over the Treasury curve after accounting for embedded options.

ICE BofA daily closing option-adjusted spreads via FRED. Change equals the Nov. 20 close minus the Nov. 16 close. One percentage point equals 100 basis points. Bars share a 0–100 basis point scale.

CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index. Option-adjusted spreads measure the yield premium over the Treasury curve after accounting for embedded options.

Effective yields reflect the returns implied by the prices and payments of bonds in each index. The terms of any new financing would depend on the issuer and the deal. An option-adjusted spread measures the extra yield over the Treasury curve after accounting for options built into the bonds.

#5040. Czech Authorities Charge 15 Over $12M Unlicensed Crypto Casino

Czech Authorities Charge 15 Over $12M Unlicensed Crypto Casino

Czech customs officers and police have charged 15 people over BETFIN, a crypto casino that investigators say operated without a gambling license while presenting itself as a decentralized project, authorities said on Thursday.

The group's unlawful gains so far total about 267 million koruna ($12.1 million), according to a joint statement from the Czech customs service and the National Centre Against Organised Crime (NCOZ). Officers detained 20 people and searched more than 40 homes and other premises in October, in an operation involving nearly 300 customs officers and police, as well as Europol staff.

Three alleged organizers are being held in custody. Those charged are accused of participating in an organized criminal group and operating gambling without a license, and the main organizers face up to 13.5 years in prison if convicted. Authorities seized assets worth about 100 million koruna ($4.5 million), including property, vehicles, jewelry, cash and crypto.

The agencies described it as the first Czech case in which suspected illegal gambling centered on a decentralized online casino using blockchain infrastructure, smart contracts and its own token.

BETFIN presented itself as a decentralized casino with its own token traded on decentralized exchanges. Investigators hired a specialist firm to examine its smart contracts on the Polygon network, and analyzed more than 2.3 million bets placed by about 28,500 players. The project was promoted on social media, Telegram and Discord, as well as in online videos and at conferences.

Users could join in two ways, Michal Šimůnek, director of the customs service's search and supervision section, told a press conference near Prague on Thursday, according to the Czech News Agency (ČTK). They could buy tokens to play casino games such as roulette, or buy them as investors and become co-owners of the casino. Despite its decentralized branding, the group ran a centrally controlled system, he said.

A large share of player accounts were created by automated programs to inflate activity, Šimůnek said. "This created the casino's supposed profit, which was then redistributed to investors," he said, in comments translated from Czech.

Developers issued billions of tokens and steered investors to buy them off-exchange, which let the group raise money without moving the token's market price, Šimůnek added. Customs officers also found that the declared value of all tokens in circulation, more than 45 billion koruna ($2 billion), far exceeded the roughly 11 million koruna ($500,000) of liquidity on exchanges.

Czech news site Seznam Zprávy reported the raids in October, saying those detained included YouTubers who had promoted BETFIN, and that the project's token had already fallen close to zero in 2025.

The token, BET, has fallen further since. It traded at about $0.000001 on Monday, more than 99.9% below its all-time high of $0.002906, and hit a new all-time low within the past week, according to CoinGecko data. Its 24-hour trading volume was about $1,100, with both CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap putting its total supply at around 777.8 billion tokens.

NCOZ deputy director Petr Danko said using blockchain technology is not illegal, but using it outside the law is. The Czech state is the injured party, he said, because the group was required to obtain authorization to run gambling. Whether investors suffered losses will depend on the ongoing investigation, he added.

The High Prosecutor's Office in Olomouc is overseeing the case. Criminal proceedings are continuing, and authorities said they could not share further details.

Although Bitcoin has recently reclaimed the $60,000 price mark after seeing a sudden shift in market sentiments that triggered increases of over 6% in its price during the last day, momentum has slowed again, further stretching the prolonged volatility seen over the past months.

With the Bitcoin bear market still persisting, Grayscale has sparked discussions across the crypto market after drawing attention toward a major bearish milestone for the asset.

Earlier today, Grayscale revealed that Bitcoin's current bear market has lasted more than 411 days and is becoming the longest on record.

While this marks an historic milestone in the Bitcoin bear market, Grayscale further disclosed an interesting twist that makes the current bear market pretty different from previous times.

The source confirmed that this bear market has been relatively mild in terms of price losses despite lasting longer than previous downturns.

All through the current bear market, Bitcoin has only posted a price decrease 56%, suggesting that it has suffered considerably smaller losses than several previous bear markets.

This means that even though Bitcoin has spent more than a year in a bear market, its decline has not been as severe as those seen in earlier cycles.

To back the data, Grayscale showed charts comparing Bitcoin's performance across historical bear markets that ended in June 2011, December 2013, December 2017, November 2021, and the ongoing October 2025 cycle.

While the 2011, 2017 and 2021 bear cycles suffered massive losses, especially during the former when its indexed performance fell below 10, the current 2025 bear market broke historical pattern by enduring a longer period yet a comparatively modest decline in Bitcoin’s price.

#5036. Bisq 2 desktop users must update to keep trading Bitcoin

Version 2.1.16 patches a flaw in the bundled Java runtime. A separate Nov. 25 network change requires nodes to run version 2.1.14 or later.

Bisq released a security update for Bisq 2, its peer-to-peer Bitcoin trading software, on Nov. 23 and urged desktop users to install version 2.1.16 as soon as possible, even if they have no trade in progress. Version 2.1.16 fixes a flaw in the app’s bundled Java software, and Bisq says desktop users need the update to keep trading. A separate network change on Nov. 25 requires nodes to run at least 2.1.14.

In the 2.1.16 release notes, Bisq identified the flaw as Java4Shell and said it could let an attacker run code on an affected system. The release also includes a Tor security update.

After the Nov. 25 change, Bisq 2 nodes running versions older than 2.1.14 can miss offers and trade messages. Bisq announced the change in October when it released version 2.1.14. Starting Nov. 25, updated nodes will require newer V2 signatures on the data they store and share. Bisq warns that versions below 2.1.14 will have trouble connecting and exchanging data, and the project will end support for them.

The project's headless node release notes warn that trades can stall if a node on 2.1.13 misses messages it needs to move a deal forward.

The official downloads page lists the desktop builds for Windows, macOS and Linux and provides PGP signatures and a public key for verifying the installers.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Version 2.1.16 also changes how the app handles a trade across a restart. It saves messages that arrive before the trade can process them, then applies them on startup if trading is enabled and the node meets the minimum trading version. In pre-release testing, a Bisq contributor reported completing test trades after upgrading Ubuntu nodes from 2.1.15 to a 2.1.16 release candidate. The test used nodes accessed through the API and covered trades that were already open during the upgrade.

For mobile traders, the version to check depends on the app. Bisq Easy Mobile runs its own node on Android. Its 0.15.0 release moved to the 2.1.14 core. Bisq says users still on 0.14.x can miss offers and messages or see trades stall after Nov. 25. Bisq urges users to install Bisq Easy 0.17.0, which uses the 2.1.15 core, to keep trading.

Bisq Connect on Android and iOS controls a separate desktop or headless Bisq 2 node. Users who rely on a node run by someone else need that operator to check the version and update it if it falls below the network minimum.

#5035. Saylor Spots New Role for Bitcoin

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees new ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.

According to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S. derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.

‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov. 23.

As per the guidance, these companies must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover their operating costs for at least a year.

As clarified by CFTC staff, Bitcoin and Ether can be used to meet this requirement (as well as payment stablecoins). The advisory also provides guidance on how staff interpret the current rules. It also applies to swap execution facilities (SEFs), which are platforms where counterparties trade swaps.

Bitcoin holdings worth $10 million could count for $8 million toward the annual requirement, based on the minimum 20% discount that CFTC staff said they would accept. This provides some flexibility in case Bitcoin's price falls. The discount is also called a haircut.

For Ether, the same minimum 20% haircut applies. For payment stablecoins, the haircut is 2%.

This provides some incentive for an exchange to actually hold BTC. Exchanges could hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets and use some of its value to satisfy this reserve requirement. There would be no need to sell it for USD first.

However, a futures exchange still needs to have sufficient unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover its operating costs for at least six months. Bitcoin, Ether and even payment stablecoins do not fall into this category.

The same six-month liquidity requirement applies to clearinghouses. Additionally, they need to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover a default by a clearing member.

CFTC staff also noted a potential downside for exchanges holding crypto reserves. During a market slump, there's a risk that an exchange's operating losses might rise. At the same time, the value of the Bitcoin it holds to cover those losses might fall.

So this possibility should be considered before an exchange decides whether to use Bitcoin to meet its financial resource requirements.

#5034. Strategy sells $176M in MSTR shares for STRC buybacks – What’s behind the shift?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy is making headlines, but there is something under the wraps that is raising eyebrows.

In its 23rd November Form 8-K filing, the Bitcoin [BTC] DAT revealed that the company is becoming more aggressive with its capital management strategy, particularly when it comes to its preferred stock, STRC.

In fact, between 16th and 22nd November, the company sold 1,925,676 shares of its Class A common stock (MSTR), generating $176.7 million in net proceeds.

But here’s a catch: instead of directing the entire amount towards Bitcoin purchases, Strategy used just $29.6 million to acquire 457 BTC while allocating the remaining proceeds towards repurchasing STRC shares.

At the same time, the company bought back 2,183,747 STRC shares for approximately $211.8 million during the same period, using $147 million from MSTR share sales and another $64.8 million from its USD cash balance. Naturally, this has raised an important question: why is Strategy selling one security to buy back another?

So, the difference lies in the roles of MSTR and STRC. MSTR, as we all know now, is Strategy’s common stock, offering investors exposure to its Bitcoin holdings and business performance. STRC, meanwhile, is a variable-rate perpetual preferred stock with a $100 stated value that pays regular dividends.

Therefore, Strategy aims to keep STRC trading around 99-100. When it trades below this range, buybacks can help support its market price while reducing outstanding shares and future dividend obligations.

This also explains the company’s expanded buyback capacity. On 23rd November, Strategy increased its Digital Credit Securities repurchase authorization from $3 billion to $4 billion, with approximately $1.12 billion remaining. At the same time, it continues to use its ATM program to raise capital by issuing MSTR shares.

Given such a change in plans, Strategy still continues to be the largest BTC holder, with a total of 851,305 BTC, acquired at an aggregate cost of $64.23 billion and an average purchase price of $75,446 per BTC.

All in all, the filing shows that Strategy is balancing Bitcoin accumulation with preferred stock buybacks rather than directing all its capital towards BTC purchases.

This comes as the MSTR stock was trading at $84.40 at press time up by 8.48% in the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, STRC was trading at $98.26 at press time up by 5.01% in the past trading day.

Lastly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also highlighted this shift, as its MSTR shares were facing mounting pressure from Bitcoin’s decline, losing over 40% in Q4 2026.

However, one thing is clear, and that is continued MSTR weakness could make fresh capital raises more difficult, threatening Strategy’s future Bitcoin accumulation plans.

#5033. Strategy Buys $30M in Bitcoin, Moves $1B From USD Reserve to Cash Pot

Strategy Buys $30M in Bitcoin, Moves $1B From USD Reserve to Cash Pot

Strategy bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million last week and moved $1 billion out of the reserve that backs its dividend payments into a general-purpose cash account, the company said on Monday.

The Bitcoin treasury firm paid an average of $64,898 per coin between November 16 and November 22, according to an SEC filing. Its fourth straight weekly purchase lifted its holdings to 851,305 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.23 billion at an average of about $75,446 per coin.

Strategy has acquired 457 $BTC and repurchased $212M of $STRC. We increased our Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program by $1B and reallocated $1B from our USD Reserve to USD Cash. As of 11/22/26, we hold 851,305 BTC and $4.8B of USD Assets. $MSTR https://t.co/Wklom6dzrm

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) November 23, 2026

At the current Bitcoin price of about $61,233, per Decrypt data, those holdings are worth about $52.1 billion, roughly $12.1 billion less than Strategy paid. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,298 over the weekend, its lowest level since September 2024.

Executive chairman Michael Saylor tweeted that, as of November 22, Strategy held 851,305 BTC and $4.8 billion in U.S. dollar assets.

Strategy's board authorized management to move up to $1 billion from its USD Reserve, which is meant to cover dividends on its preferred stock and interest on its debt, to its USD Cash account. Management can use that account for broader purposes, including buying Bitcoin, topping up the reserve and other capital management.

After the move, the USD Reserve stood at $3.73 billion and USD Cash at $1.09 billion. The reserve held $4.77 billion on November 8, according to an earlier filing. Strategy drew $17.6 million from it to pay preferred dividends last week.

Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock, for $211.8 million, down from $228 million the week before. It funded the Bitcoin purchase and $147 million of the buyback by selling 1,925,676 shares of MSTR stock for $176.7 million in net proceeds, and paid the remaining $64.8 million from USD Cash.

The board also raised the cap on its digital credit securities repurchase program, which covers its preferred stock, from $3 billion to $4 billion, leaving $1.12 billion available. Before the increase, about $120 million remained, after two weeks of STRC buybacks totaling about $440 million. Another $1 billion remains available to buy back MSTR stock.

The changes come a week before index provider MSCI removes MSTR from its MSCI USA Index after trading closes on November 30, which also takes it out of broader benchmarks such as the MSCI World index. Strategy has estimated that funds linked to MSCI indexes hold about 13 million of its shares.

#5032. BlackRock drives Bitcoin ETFs to worst month on record as crypto fund withdrawals near $6 billion

BlackRock's flagship Bitcoin and Ethereum funds have recorded $4.9 billion in November outflows, with four trading sessions remaining.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have recorded their worst month since launching in January 2024, led by unprecedented withdrawals from BlackRock.

Data from Farside Investors shows that the funds registered $569.69 million in net outflows on Nov. 23, pushing November's withdrawals to $4.71 billion. This surpasses the previous monthly record of $4.51 billion set in June by approximately $200 million.

Meanwhile, US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $84.92 million in withdrawals on Monday, bringing their monthly outflows to $1.15 billion.

Together, the investment products have registered $5.86 billion in net withdrawals this month, reflecting deteriorating demand for crypto exposure through traditional financial markets.

The latest withdrawals came despite Monday's crypto market rally after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive officer briefly lifted Bitcoin above $64,000. The top crypto has pared back these gains and is trading at $60.065 as of press time, per CryptoSlate's data.

According to Farside Investors, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led Monday's withdrawals with $509.3 million, accounting for approximately 89% of the day's net outflows. Grayscale's Bitcoin Mini Trust and Bitwise's BITB followed with withdrawals of $61.08 million and $12.6 million, respectively.

Fidelity's FBTC was the only Bitcoin fund to attract fresh capital, registering $13.29 million in net inflows.

BlackRock has emerged as the epicenter of November's crypto ETF withdrawals, with IBIT recording nearly $4 billion in monthly net outflows, its highest since inception.

The withdrawals represent approximately 85% of the combined outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs this month. IBIT has recorded withdrawals in 15 of November's 16 trading sessions.

Notably, the pace of redemptions has accelerated considerably over the past three trading sessions.

IBIT registered a then-record $541.1 million outflow on Nov. 19 before surpassing that figure with another $544.7 million in withdrawals on Nov. 20.

Combined with Monday's outflows, investors have pulled nearly $1.6 billion from the BlackRock fund over three consecutive trading sessions, representing about 40% of its monthly withdrawals.

Similar redemption pressure has extended to BlackRock's Ethereum investment products.

According to Farside Investors, the asset manager's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) registered $90.5 million in net outflows on Monday, bringing its monthly outflows to around $977 million. Notably, BlackRock’s staked Ether fund (ETHB) has also registered more than $90 million in outflows this month.

#5031. XRP Ledger Volume Per Account Up 437% as Trades Get Bigger

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Each account trading on the XRP Ledger's decentralized exchange moved an average of 4,328 XRP a day in the third quarter of 2026, up 437% from 805 XRP in the same quarter a year earlier, according to a report that XRP treasury company Evernorth released on Tuesday.

According to Evernorth, the average swap on the XRP Ledger reached 35 XRP in the third quarter, up from 19 XRP in the second quarter and under 6 XRP a year earlier. "The growth came from bigger trades, not more of them," the company wrote in the report.

At the same time, the number of accounts trading on the XRP Ledger's order book fell to 1,042 a day in the third quarter of 2026 from 2,027 a day in the third quarter of 2025. The number stood at 1,203 in the fourth quarter of 2025, 1,324 in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,125 in the second quarter, according to the report.

Order-book volume on the XRP Ledger rose to 4.51 million XRP a day in the third quarter from 1.63 million XRP a day a year earlier, Evernorth data shows.

In total, 5.16 million XRP a day was traded on the XRP Ledger's exchange in the third quarter, and the figure was up 96% year over year, according to Evernorth.

Measured in U.S. dollars, exchange volume on the XRP Ledger fell 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the report.

Evernorth also compared the XRP Ledger with Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche and Polygon. Across these seven networks, exchange volume in dollars fell 42% over the same period, the report shows.

XRP was trading at around $0.93 on Tuesday morning after reaching as high as $1.026 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap.

The report also shows that the average balance of Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger reached $937 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $539 million in the second quarter. By the end of the quarter, the RLUSD balance on the XRP Ledger stood at $1.15 billion, compared with $670 million at the end of the second quarter, and the number of RLUSD holders on the network rose to 67,449 from 45,620.

According to Evernorth, the XRP Ledger's average share of RLUSD reached 48.5% in the third quarter, up from 34% in the second quarter. Still, Ethereum finished the quarter with more RLUSD than the XRP Ledger. Evernorth noted that on Ethereum, RLUSD "can already be lent," and that on the XRP Ledger, "native lending is in validator voting."

As of Nov. 20, the Lending Protocol amendment had 24 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. The amendment needs 29 votes, held for 14 days, to activate.

Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9, and its shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN on Oct. 12. The company entered the public markets holding approximately 473 million XRP, according to its press release.

Evernorth announced the deal in October 2025, with investments from SBI, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

#5030. Morning Minute: Crypto Rebounds after NVDA Drives Friday Selloff

Morning Minute: Crypto Rebounds after NVDA Drives Friday Selloff

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down 47.5% from its October high, which works out to roughly $2.7 trillion of market value gone in seven weeks. The company beat earnings last week and guided revenue higher, and the stock still fell 23% across the five sessions.

The Nasdaq dropped 10% on the week, its worst since 2020, erasing its entire 2026 gain and shedding about $8.7 trillion since October 6. The S&P and Dow both closed in correction, AMD lost 20.5%, and CoreWeave now trades below its IPO price. Bank of America’s fund manager survey showed investors cutting tech exposure by the most since 2006, with 52% expecting at least one major hyperscaler to announce a capex cut inside six months.

Polymarket traders put 54% odds that the AI bubble will burst in 2026.

Crypto rode the same elevator down. Bitcoin hit roughly $55,100 Friday night, its lowest level since 2024 and marking a new cycle low, 56% off last October’s peak. Fear and Greed printed 9 and ETFs bled $1.79 billion on the week. It’s now tracking toward two consecutive down years, which has never happened before.

Then came the weekend bounce. Bitcoin reclaimed $60,000 and sits over $61,000 this morning; ETH is back above $1,710, and even Anthropic, down 9% Friday, quotes near $90 on Hyperliquid’s perp, still above its $83 offer.

Two explanations landed over the weekend.

U.S. President Donald Trump posted Sunday that the market is down $6 trillion since the Democrats’ “rather strange” win on November 3, that the Nasdaq is down 20%, and that it’s “100% due to” Democratic policy. Looks like no Trump bailout is coming anytime soon.

Elon Musk’s version is more useful. He warned Saturday that the cash shortage next year is “going to be nuts,” because even a few months of lag between paying for compute and earning revenue off it means hundreds of billions in incremental working capital. Then the question: where will that come from?

That’s a funding problem rather than a valuation one, and it lands harder coming from him. SpaceX reportedly sold $32 billion of bonds last week to buy Nvidia chips, so he’s describing a squeeze he’s already borrowing into.

So where does this leave us? The Fed meets December 8th and 9th with the market pricing a hike into all of this. Gas prices just hit an eight-month low ahead of Thanksgiving, down about 15% in a month, which should take some pressure off the headline print. The catch is that pump prices are still running 18% above last year, and core CPI, the number Waller actually cited when he floated fifty basis points, strips energy out entirely. Any relief has to come from shelter and services cooling instead.

Perhaps the Fed provides some. Whether it’s enough to stop the bleeding, only time will tell.

#5026. LINK, AAVE and UNI Now Supported by Fidelity

Fidelity Investments now supports three new cryptocurrencies on its retail crypto trading platform: Chainlink (LINK), Aave (AAVE) and Uniswap (UNI).

The firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov. 24. In just one day, Fidelity added the same number of digital assets that it had added in the four years since it first made Bitcoin and Ether available for customer trading.

Eligible U.S. customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app. Some states may have limited access to Fidelity's services.

Fidelity's three new listings include tokens that represent different areas of decentralized finance. Aave is a lending protocol where users can deposit crypto assets to earn interest or use them as collateral for loans. AAVE token holders can vote on changes to the protocol's lending markets and other aspects of its operation.

Uniswap is a decentralized trading platform where users can trade different tokens using shared pools of assets provided by other users. UNI is the Uniswap governance token.

Chainlink provides the data that blockchain apps need to operate. For example, a lending protocol might use a Chainlink price feed to assess the value of collateral for a borrower's loan. Chainlink (LINK) tokens are used to pay for services provided on its network.

Fidelity Crypto started accepting customers from its waitlist in November 2022. At the time, the only two cryptocurrencies it offered were Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH). By March 2023, Fidelity was offering its service to more eligible U.S. investors, but these were still the only cryptocurrencies it allowed customers to trade.

On July 17, 2024, Fidelity added Litecoin (LTC) to its list of cryptocurrencies, bringing the total to three. Over a year later, on Oct. 23, 2025, the company introduced Solana (SOL). In addition to individual retail accounts, Solana became available for crypto IRAs, wealth managers and institutional clients.

Fidelity added its fifth cryptocurrency on Feb. 4, 2026, when it launched Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD) as its first stablecoin available to retail and institutional investors. Eligible users can exchange or redeem each FIDD token for $1. Fidelity waives its usual crypto trading fee when users exchange FIDD for dollars.
